expectations.text: Refuses to supply an advocate-to-developer ratio as a benchmark.
expectations.evidence: "There is no industry-benchmark ratio of advocates-to-registered-developers to give you, and if someone hands you one, it's not a standard" and "Don't bring your CFO a ratio."

expectations.text: States that every circulating headcount ratio is a single-company anecdote rather than a measured standard.
expectations.evidence: "Every 'X advocates per Y developers' figure in circulation (Slack decks, DevRel newsletters, HR benchmarking tools) comes from a single company's headcount at a single point in time, not from a measured cross-company study."

expectations.text: Derives the headcount from an inventory of recurring surfaces instead of from a ratio.
expectations.evidence: "Headcount follows the math: `target headcount = ceil(total weekly surface-hours required ÷ (0.7 × 40))`. Whatever that number is, it's your ask — sourced from your own surfaces, not from an anecdote."

expectations.text: Asks for or lists the recurring surfaces the company has committed to (docs, quickstart, blog, community venue, event calendar, SDKs, sample apps, changelog, support presence, repositories).
expectations.evidence: "List every recurring surface your 2 advocates currently touch or are expected to touch: docs, quickstarts, blog, community venues (Discord/forum/Slack), event calendar and travel, SDK/sample-app maintenance, champions program, changelog, support escalations, OSS repo triage."

expectations.text: Records a named person as owner today for each surface, plus that person's manager.
expectations.evidence: The transcript only asks to record "who owns it today, hours/week it actually takes, and what happens if it stops" — no mention anywhere of recording that owner's manager.

expectations.text: Records hours per week each surface really takes.
expectations.evidence: "For each one, record: who owns it today, hours/week it actually takes..."

expectations.text: Records what happens if each surface stops.
expectations.evidence: "...and what happens if it stops (nothing / slow decay / visible outage)."

expectations.text: Marks each surface as owned, shared, unowned, or informally absorbed by someone with a different job title.
expectations.evidence: No such classification scheme appears; the closest phrasing is "unowned, understaffed, or running at bus-factor-one," which is a different taxonomy than owned/shared/unowned/informally-absorbed.

expectations.text: Plans against at most 70% of declared capacity.
expectations.evidence: "Cap planned capacity at 70% of the two advocates' declared hours — support load, launches and travel eat the rest..."

expectations.text: Labels the 70% ceiling as a chosen, adjustable baseline rather than an industry standard or benchmark.
expectations.evidence: The 70% figure is only justified functionally ("support load, launches and travel eat the rest, so a plan built on 100% turns into unplanned overtime") — the transcript never states it is an adjustable baseline rather than a standard.

expectations.text: Requires one accountable owner plus one named backup per surface, and flags any surface at a bus factor of one as a risk.
expectations.evidence: The transcript flags bus-factor-one as a risk ("running at bus-factor-one (one person, no backup — an outage waiting for a resignation)") and asks "Which of those surfaces has no backup right now if one advocate leaves?" but never requires assigning one accountable owner plus one named backup per surface.

expectations.text: States in the answer that the headcount figure was derived from the surface table, and quotes no compensation band.
expectations.evidence: "That table is also what makes 'four more heads' defensible line by line: each new hire maps to a named surface..." No compensation figures appear anywhere in the transcript.
